title: 1959 AHSME Problem 2
statement: Through a point \(P\) inside triangle \(ABC\) a line is drawn parallel to the base \(\overline{AB},\) dividing the triangle into two equal areas. If the altitude to \(\overline{AB}\) has length \(1,\) then the distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AB}\) is:

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the requested distance. The triangle above the parallel line is similar to the original triangle, with linear ratio \(1-x.\) Its area is half the original area, so \[ (1-x)^2=\frac12. \] Since \(0\lt x\lt1,\) we have \(1-x=\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\) and therefore \[ x=1-\frac1{\sqrt2}=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{2}. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(x\) be the distance from \(P\) to the base
The small triangle above the parallel line has altitude \(1-x\) and half the original area
